newsitem.title: USA: L.A. forms committee to study city utility options.
newsitem.headline: L.A. forms committee to study city utility options.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council on Wednesday established a committee to review a motion to amend the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power's (LADWP) plans to select a strategic partner.

The municipal utility's general manager still plans to sumbit to the LADWP board on Tuesday a final recommendation for an out-of-state power marketing partner, according to LADWP spokeswoman Karen Denne.
The three finalists for a strategic alliance with the muncipal utility are the Duke/Louis Dreyfus partnership, PacifiCorp and Enron Corp.
If the board approves the final selection, the matter will then be submitted to the City Council for final acceptance, Denne said.

But Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, with the strong support of Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan, is asking to re-open the selection process so that it can submit a petition to ally with LADWP.
"We are happy to see that the council took the action it did today," said an Edison spokesman.
A spokeswoman for Duke Power in Charlotte, N.C., would not comment on the LADWP solicitation, while officials at PacifiCorp and Enron could not be reached.
The first meeting of the council's new committee on energy restructuring will be held Friday.
